chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub al-Ahmar, from Abu Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man: is it permissible for him to have intercourse with his wife's slave girl? He said, 'No, until she gifts her to him.' Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) had ruled in this matter that a woman came seeking enforcement of judgment against her husband, and she said, 'He has had intercourse with my slave girl and made her pregnant.' The man said, 'She merely gifted herself to me.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Bring me proof, otherwise I will stone you.' When the woman saw that stoning was not less than that [i.e., if he claimed gift, he would be stoned for intercourse with a non-wife], she admitted that she had gifted him, so Ali (peace be upon him) gave her a flogging as a fixed punishment and upheld that [right] for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a husband to have intercourse with his wife's slave girl according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a man’s right to intercourse with his wife’s slave girl is contingent upon a formal gift (hibah), citing a judicial precedent from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the burden of proof. In this case, Ali (peace be upon him) required concrete evidence for the husband’s claim of gift, threatening stoning if unproven, which led to the wife’s admission and the husband’s upheld right, illustrating the Shia legal principle that ownership rights must be explicitly transferred rather than assumed. This narration underscores the importance of clear legal documentation in marital and slave-ownership relations within the fiqh of the Ahl al-Bayt.
